In a bowl, combine olive oil, garlic, onion powder, black pepper, Cajun seasoning and shrimp.
Mix with rubber spatula until shrimp is coated.
Preheat air fryer to 400 degrees F and spray with nonstick cooking spray, if needed.
Arrange shrimp in a single layer in air fryer and cook for 3-4 minutes Flip shrimp and continue to cook for 2-3 more minutes or until cooked through.
Serve immediately.
hints: Can be served with salad, with a pasta dish or with roasted vegetables.
Can be made with fresh shrimp, just make sure it is cooked all the way through. Cooked and uncooked shrimp shrinks when cooked.
Look for cooked shrimp with the lowest salt content.

title: Greek Yogurt Berry Parfait
description: Ingredients Preparation Helpful hints Greek yogurt has more protein than other yogurts. Can be a good substitute for eggs in the morning. You may substitute a sugar free sweetener for the honey to lower to added sugar content and make it diabetes friendly.
ingredients: 1/2 cup low fat vanilla Greek yogurt
steps: Mix lemon juice and honey into yogurt.
Place from strawberries in the bottom of a mason jar. Top with yogurt mixture.
Let the jar set in the refrigerator overnight and grab in the morning. You can stir to incorporate the berries, which after thawing will create a nice strawberry sauce.
hints: Greek yogurt has more protein than other yogurts. Can be a good substitute for eggs in the morning.
You may substitute a sugar free sweetener for the honey to lower to added sugar content and make it diabetes friendly.

title: Garden Vegetable Pita
description: Enjoy a quick, healthy, and delicious meal with our Veggie and Mozzarella Pitas
steps: Rough chop bell pepper, zucchini and onion. Mince garlic. Heat olive oil in skillet. Add chopped vegetables and garlic. Cook and stir for about 10 minutes.
Add the vegetables to the top of the pita. Evenly divide mozzarella, torn or sliced into pieces, among each pita and fold up like a taco.
Alternatively, split pita in half. Divide vegetables evenly each of the 8 pita halves. Evenly divide mozzarella, torn or sliced into pieces, among each pita.
hints: The naturally occurring phosphorus in foods like fresh cheese, are only partly absorbed by our bodies. Approximately 40-60%, each food and person are different.
You can find fresh mozzarella in a slices log. Tear or slice to your likely in the pita.

title: Veggie Topped Polenta
description: Enjoy a vibrant and satisfying meal with this easy-to-make DaVita recipe that includes polenta and veggies.
serving_size: 2 polenta slices, 3/4 cup vegetable mix and 1 ounce cheese
ingredients: 12 ounces pre-cooked polenta, from 24 ounces roll
4-ounces fresh pre-sliced mozzarella 4 tablespoons DaVita’s Easy Honey Mustard Balsamic Vinaigrette
steps: Roughly chop bell pepper and zucchini. Heat olive oil in skillet. Add chopped vegetables and heat for about 5 minutes. Add beans and cook and stir for about 5 to 8 minutes longer.
Spray a second pan with cooking spray and heat on medium. Slice the polenta into 8 slices and brown in the skillet. About 4 minutes per side.

To serve, place 2 slices of polenta on a plate and add approximately 3/4 cup of veggies on top. Tear apart, or cut up, fresh mozzarella, should be about 1 ounce per serving. Top with 1 tablespoon of dressing. Save the rest of the dressing for a salad or as a raw vegetable dip.
hints: The naturally occurring phosphorus in foods like fresh cheese are only partly absorbed by our bodies. Approximately 40-60%, each food and person is different.
Pre-cooked polenta usually comes in a 24-ounce tube. Use half for this recipe and save the rest for later use.
To make it more diabetes-friendly, you may cut back on the cheese to reduce the fat content.

title: Tilapia with Grilled Pineapple Salsa
description: Try our simple baked tilapia, perfectly complemented by a tangy grilled pineapple salsa. A kidney-friendly delight!
steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Prepare DaVita’s Grilled Pineapple Salsa. Set aside.
Cover a baking sheet with foil and spray with non-stick cooking spray. Brush each fillet evenly with olive oil and sprinkle with pepper.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, until fish is fork tender and flakes. Place each fillet on a plate and top with 1/4 cup of the Grilled Pineapple Salsa.
hints: Naturally occurring potassium is only partially absorbed by our bodies. Approximately 40-60%, each food and/or person is different in what they absorb.
You may substitute tilapia with other white fish that you prefer.

title: Crunchy Southwestern Breakfast Wrap
description: A delicious, protein-packed breakfast wrap. Ground meat, fluffy eggs and potatoes folded in a tortilla and seared to a golden-brown.
steps: Shred potatoes. Bring a pot of water to a boil and add potatoes, cooking for 10-15 minutes. Drain and rinse and repeat boiling once more time. Drain.

Heat 3 Tbsp vegetable oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Spread the shredded potatoes out in thin layer throughout the pan. Cook until crispy and golden, about 3-4 minutes per side, flipping with a spatula. Remove from pan and set aside.

In the same pan over medium heat, add lean ground meat. Add paprika, garlic powder, ground black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Cook for about 7 minutes, frequently turning with spatula for even browning until meat has reached 160 °F. Drain and dispose of excess oil. Remove meat from pan and set aside.
Heat 1 Tbsp of vegetable oil in the same pan over low heat. Crack and whisk eggs in a small bowl. Add to pan and scramble until eggs are set but not hard (145°F).
Warm the tortillas in a clean, large skillet over medium heat, about 30 seconds each side. Tortillas should be bendable.

Divide potatoes, ground meat, eggs, and cheese into the center of each tortilla. Fold the top of the tortilla towards the center and then fold each corner up to the center moving clockwise until you have a closed wrap (5 folds).
Add 1 Tbsp vegetable oil to the large skillet over medium heat. Heat each wrap for about 30 seconds on each side until golden brown.
hints: Ground beef can be replaced with ground chicken or turkey. Egg whites or egg substitute (avoid those with phosphorus additives) can be used in place of whole eggs.
Wraps can be prepared ahead of time and reheated in the morning. They can last in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days, or frozen and reheated.
Can substitute chicken, remove the wrap and remove cheddar cheese for a lower fat, diabetes-friendly meal.

title: Chicken, Fruit and Poppyseed Salad
description: Looking for a healthy and delicious meal? Try this easy-to-make chicken salad with a twist of fruit and a flavorful sugar-free poppyseed dressing.
ingredients: 1/4 cup pineapple chunks, fresh or canned
steps: Cut salad into bite size pieces, drain mandarin oranges. If you use canned pineapple, drain pineapple.
Slice cooked chicken breast into strips. Layer lettuce, fruit and chicken in a medium bowl. Top with dressing.
hints: A left-over cooked grilled or roasted chicken breast works great with this recipe and creates an easy lunch. Use half a chicken breast if on a lower protein diet.
A different vinaigrette can be used. Look for dressing that has less than 200 mg of sodium per 2 tablespoon serving.

title: Pad Thai
description: Craving homemade Pad Thai? Get our simple, kidney-friendly, recipe for perfectly cooked noodles and a savory sauce.
ingredients: 4 ounces of rice noodles or glass noodles for gluten free
8 ounces chicken breast (other optional choices: tofu or peeled/deveined shrimp)
steps: Soak the rice noodles by placing them in a shallow pan and cover with boiling water for 4-7 minutes, stirring occasionally until al dente; drain, rinse with cold water.

Finely chop onion and roughly chop garlic. Whisk the two eggs in a bowl with a fork and set aside. Make the Pad Thai Sauce: whisk fish sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar and coconut aminos in a small bowl. Set aside.

Slice chicken into very thin strips. (If using tofu: Blot tofu with paper towels pressing down firmly. Cut tofu into ¾ inch cubes, and for extra crispy tofu, dredge in a little corn starch. If using shrimp: Pat dry with paper towel.)
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large saucepan or wok, over medium-high heat. Sear the seasoned chicken (If using shrimp or tofu cook the same until cooked through.) Set aside.

Heat a little more oil in the wok or large skillet over medium heat, add onion & garlic and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Scoot the onion mixture to the side, add more oil, and pour in the eggs. Scramble and break them apart into little bits and move them to the side. Add more oil, and the noodles, sauté 2-3 minutes until the noodles are soft and pliable and even a little crispy.
Add Pad Thai Sauce and stir everything together and cook 1-2 minutes, then add the cooked chicken (shrimp or tofu) and sauté until warm. Squeeze with a little lime juice. Turn off heat.
Toss in 1/2 the bean sprouts. Give one more toss and serve immediately. Divide between two plates. May add chili flake and/or scallions as an optional topping.
hints: Coconut aminos vary in sodium, choose the lowest you can find. Cut back noodles and use a sugar substitute in place of brown sugar to make this more diabetes friendly.
This dish is a bit higher in sodium but is about ½ of a take-out Pad Thai meal, which can reach around 1300 mg of sodium.

title: Hamburger Salad
description: Enjoy all the classic flavors of a cheeseburger in this quick and easy salad! The limited amount of cheese, helps keep it kidney-friendly.
steps: Mix mayonnaise, mustard, chopped pickles, vinegar, sugar, chopped onion and paprika and set aside.
Heat sauté pan on medium and add beef, breaking up clumps until cooked through. Add pepper and mix in pan.
While beef is cooking, chop lettuce and slice onion.
When ready to serve mix lettuce, cheese and onion. This can be divided into 4 bowls, or you can store any unused portions.
Add about a 1/4 of beef to each bowl and drizzle with dressing. Serve right away.
hints: You can store the ingredients separately and use them as leftovers. If on a lower protein diet use only 8 ounces of beef.
May use light mayonnaise but look for the lowest sodium version.

title: Burrito Bowl
description: Looking for a fresh and easy weeknight dinner? This kidney-friendly chicken burrito bowl recipe features a zesty chipotle dressing.
ingredients: 2 boneless, skinless chicken thighs (or chicken breast)
steps: Combine all dressing ingredients into a food processor or blender, and blend until well combined (should yield 1 1/4 cups).
Season chicken thighs with 1/4 cup of dressing, brush on both sides.
Grill seasoned chicken on grill, or inside on grill pan until cooked through. Cut into slices. Slice peppers, onion, and zucchini into thin strips.
Place 1-1/2 tablespoons oil into medium sauté pan, heat over medium heat, add onions, peppers, and zucchini slices.
Sauté vegetables for 3 minutes on medium heat, add in onion and garlic powder, and stir until vegetables are equally seasoned. Cook vegetables until tender.
Cook white rice according to package directions to yield one cup. Slice lettuce into thin strips.

Prepare bowls by adding 1 cup lettuce, 1/2 cup sliced chicken, 1/4 cup white rice, 1/4 cup sautéed vegetables and top with 3 tablespoons dressing to each bowl. Optional, may top each bowl with 2 tortilla chips if desired.
hints: Cooking spray can be used in place of olive oil to cook the vegetables. A sugar substitute can be used in place of the honey for diabetes friendly dressing.

The potassium in this dish is higher but comes from natural sources like vegetables. Our bodies only absorb about 40-60%. Vegetables also provide other nutrients and fiber. This is also a one-dish meal.

If desired; you could add 1/4 cup low sodium canned black beans (rinsed and drained).This would roughly add about 80 mg sodium, 180 mg potassium and 64 mg phosphorus. Keeping in mind with naturally occurring potassium/phosphorus like found in beans, our bodies only absorb about 40-60% of those nutrients.

title: Tuna Melt Sandwich
description: Enjoy a delicious and kidney-friendly tuna melt! This easy-to-make recipe features low-sodium tuna and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 8 ounces low sodium or unsalted tuna (two 5-ounce cans)
steps: Drain tuna. Mix mayonnaise, black pepper and tuna in a bowl. Evenly divide mixture between hamburger bun bottoms.
Place cheese on top of tuna mixture, preheat oven to 350F. Place tuna half and top of the bun (face up) on a baking sheet. Bake for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile slice cucumber, green pepper and red onion. Shred or chop lettuce. Remove sandwiches from oven and layer vegetables evenly on top. Plate and serve. May save the second sandwich for another day or share with family or friends.
hints: This recipe is higher in potassium, but it is naturally occurring from vegetables and tuna. From vegetables sources our bodies only absorb about 40-60% of the natural potassium.
If you are on a lower protein diet, you may cut back on the amount of tuna by half or a third.

title: Strawberry Milkshake
description: Satisfy your sweet tooth with this treat! This creamy strawberry drink is a kidney-friendly decadent milkshake and is also sugar-free.
steps: Place all ingredients in a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into fun glass, garnish with a strawberry, and enjoy!
hints: The heavy cream can be replaced with coconut cream for a dairy free option.
Refrigerated coconut milk is located near the milk alternatives in the store cooler.

title: Baked Donuts 5 Ways
description: Bake a batch of delicious homemade donuts today! This easy recipe bakes in just minutes and you can customize with your favorite toppings.
ingredients: Cinnamon and Sugar: Combine 1 cup of granulated white sugar and 1 tablespoon of cinnamon in a gallon zip bag. Add warm donuts to the bag, seal and shake gently to coat.

Classic Glazed: Combine1 cup of powdered sugar, 1/3 cup of non-dairy milk, 1/2 teaspoon of pure vanilla extract in a bowl. Whisk until smooth. Dunk warm donuts in glaze. Let rest on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes to dry.

Maple Coffee Glaze: Combine 1-1/2 cups of powdered sugar, 1 teaspoon maple extract, 1/2 cup brewed coffee, and 2 tablespoons melted butter. Whisk until smooth. Dunk warm donuts in glaze. Let rest on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes to dry.

Berry Frosted: Combine 1 cup of powdered sugar, 2 tablespoons of berry jam (strawberry, raspberry, or blueberry), and 1 teaspoon of water. Whisk until smooth. Dunk warm donuts in frosting and set on wire rack. Let dry 30 minutes.

Confetti Frosted: Combine 1 cup of powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon of non-dairy milk, and 1-2 drops of food coloring. Whisk until smooth. Dunk warm donuts in frosting and set on wire rack. Top with sprinkles. Let dry 30 minutes.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Lightly grease two standard donut pans or a standard muffin tin (see hint).
In a mixing bowl, beat butter, vegetable oil, brown sugar, and 1/2 cup granulated sugar until smooth. Add eggs, beat together.
Stir in baking powder, baking soda, 1/2 to 1 teaspoon cinnamon, salt, and vanilla.
Alternate adding flour and milk into mixture beginning and ending with flour until combined. The batter will be thick.
Spoon batter into tin, filling 3/4 of the way up. Bake for 10-12 minutes. Remove, and wait for 5-7 minutes to cool slightly. Flip on to a wire rack.
Prepare toppings of your choice (or multiple toppings). Each topping makes enough for 12 donuts.
Store in an air-tight container for up to 3 days.
hints: No donut pan? Take a long piece of foil (about 9in). Fold into long rectangle and then create a circle the size of your desired donut hole. Repeat 12 times. Place into each space of your muffin tin. Center the foil and spoon batter around the foil.
Don’t care about the donut shape? Just bake in a muffin tin. You will need to add 3-4 minutes to back time. Each topping makes enough for 12 donuts.

title: Sausage, Egg and Cheese Bagel Thin
description: The easy, kidney-friendly breakfast can be a quick meal, morning or evening.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon shredded natural sharp cheddar cheese
steps: In a small skillet sprayed with nonstick cooking spray, pour egg and cook and scramble over medium low heat. When egg appears almost cooked through, turn over with a spatula and cook an additional 30 seconds.
Toast bagel thins.
Place turkey sausage patty on a plate, cover with a paper towel and cook in the microwave for 1 minute or the time recommended on package.
Assemble cooked egg on bagel thin (fold to fit bagel thins). Top with sausage patty, then sharp cheddar cheese and remaining bagel thin half.
hints: Sandwiches can be prepared ahead of time and reheated in the morning. They can last in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
This recipe is lower in sodium than similar fast foods sandwiches. They can range from ~900-1490 mg of sodium.

title: Breaded Fish Sandwich
description: Enjoy a crispy, oven-baked cod fillet sandwich, a delicious alternative to a classic fried fish sandwich, while providing 26 g of protein.
ingredients: 1/8 teaspoon ground pepper, or to taste
steps: Thaw fish according to package directions. May also use fresh cod if desired.
Preheat oven to 450F. Line a baking sheet with foil and spray with non-stick cooking spray.
Add crackers to a zip top bag and crush with a rolling pin or crush between your hands. Add paprika and pepper, then pour out onto a medium size plate.
Add the flour to a shallow bowl. Beat the egg in a separate bowl.
Take one fillet and lay in flour coating both sides. Then do the same in the egg covering both sides. Finally cover with crackers crumbs all around the fish.

Lay on prepared sheet pan and repeat with second fillet. Bake for 4-5 minutes, flip the fish over and bake 4-5 minutes longer. Cook to an internal temperature of at least 145F. Serve on hamburger bun.
hints: Top with a teaspoon of mustard or other low sodium condiment. See our Sauces & Seasonings Category on our recipe page for other topping ideas.
Serve with coleslaw, fresh side salad or steamed vegetables.

title: Angel Food Sherbet Cake
description: This easy Angel Food Sherbet Cake uses just three ingredients and is a delicious dessert that can fit into a kidney-friendly diet.
ingredients: One 16-ounce tub sugar free non-dairy whipped topping
Store bought Angel Food cake (or homemade)
steps: Defrost whipped topping and sherbet.
Cut the cake horizontally in the middle to create a top and bottom section of the cake.
Spread sherbet generously across bottom half of cake, ~ 4-5 inches thick. Place top of cake on the sherbet.
Frost all the cake with whipped topping. Place in freezer for 4-6 hours. Remove from freezer when ready to serve.
hints: Look for store-bought angel food cake with no or minimal phosphorus additives in the ingredient list.
May use regular whipped topping, but it will increase the added sugar by ~20 grams or more.
This dessert is an occasional treat, would not be appropriate for people with diabetes
May try different flavors of sherbet if desired.

title: Beach Boy Omelet
description: Want to feel like you’re at the beach while eating a kidney-friendly breakfast? Look no further—the Beach Boy Omelet is here for your kidney diet needs.
steps: Chop onion and green pepper. Shred potato.
Heat oil in a nonstick skillet. Add onion and green pepper; sauté for 2 minutes. Add shredded potatoes and cook for 5 minutes until browned, turning once. Remove from skillet and set aside.
Spray skillet with oil and heat over medium heat. Beat eggs with non-dairy creamer and pour into skillet. Cook until eggs are set.
Place shredded potatoes in the center of the omelet. Fold both sides of the omelet over with a spatula, then slide onto a plate.
Garnish with parsley sprigs and season to taste.
hints: For a lower potassium omelet, soak fresh or frozen shredded potatoes in 2 cups of water for 2 hours. Place on a clean kitchen towel, cover and roll up to remove excess water before cooking. This reduces the potassium content by approximately 43 milligrams.

title: Garden Salad
description: This easy salad can add a touch of color to your meal.
steps: Rinse lettuce leaves in hot water for 5 seconds, then immediately rinse in cold water. Drain and cut into small pieces.
Shred carrot. Cut celery and bell pepper into julienne strips.
Sauté corn kernels in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat for a few minutes until tender and golden. Remove and let cool.
In a cup, mix the remaining 3 tablespoons oil, lemon juice and pepper.
Combine everything in 1 large bowl, add the vinaigrette and toss. Serve immediately.
hints: Choose olive oil for salads and vegetables; you may leave the vinaigrette off the salad. Vinegar may be substituted for the olive oil.

title: Beef and Vegetable Soup
description: Stews and soups are traditional comfort foods. Beef and Vegetable Soup is a kidney-friendly soup with all the delicious flavor of the soup Mom used to make.
steps: Peel carrot and bell pepper.
Wash all vegetables and chop into small pieces.
Peel potato and cut into pieces. Place in a pan and cover completely with water. Bring to a boil and drain. Repeat the process and set aside.
Trim lean beef and cut into small pieces.
Crush garlic cloves.
Place a pot with enough water to cook the ingredients over high heat and add the ingredients.
Stir constantly for 30 minutes until the ingredients are cooked.
Serve hot.
hints: Boiling potatoes twice reduces their potassium content.

title: Breaded Shrimp
description: Breaded Shrimp is a recipe that adds extra flavor to shrimp of any size. Instead of a flour batter, this recipe calls for a cornstarch batter followed by a coating of bread crumbs.
steps: Clean shrimp, remove shells, devein and cut open along the back to butterfly.
Add pepper, garlic and lemon juice.
Preheat oil in a skillet.
In a bowl, mix cornstarch, water and eggs.
Dip shrimp one at a time so they are completely coated with the batter.
Roll in bread crumbs.
Fry shrimp until golden brown.
hints: For extra seasoning, try adding cayenne pepper.

title: Watermelon Summer Cooler
description: Cool off with this kidney-friendly recipe – Watermelon Summer Cooler.
steps: Place all ingredients except the garnish slices in a blender and blend for 30 seconds.
Pour into 2 small glasses, garnish with watermelon slices and enjoy!
hints: Watermelons vary in sweetness. Adjust by adding sweetener if needed.
For fluid-restricted diets, enjoy a Watermelon Summer Cooler now and freeze a serving for later. Remove from freezer 10 to 15 minutes before serving.
If you use a sugar substitute instead of sugar, carbohydrates are reduced by 6 grams and calories to 26 per 6-ounce serving.

title: Baked Chicken
description: This kidney-friendly chicken dish gets its flavor from garlic and spices, and the olive oil helps keep the chicken moist.
steps: Preheat oven to 177° C. Coat baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place chicken breasts on the baking sheet.
Finely mince garlic.
In a small container, combine pepper, olive oil, lemon juice and garlic. Mix together well.
Spread lemon mixture over the chicken breasts.
Sprinkle paprika evenly over the chicken breasts and bake for 35 minutes or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165° F or 74° C.
Let chicken breasts rest, covered with aluminum foil, for 10-15 minutes before slicing or serving.
hints: Natural seasonings such as oregano or bay leaf can be added for even more flavor.

title: Chicken Burritos
description: Burritos offer a meal wrapped in a tortilla. These chicken burritos from a DaVita dietitian in Colombia combine vegetables with chicken breast and cream cheese in a corn tortilla wrap.
steps: Wash lettuce very well and dry. Tear by hand into small pieces.
Cut onion, bell pepper (washed and seeded) and peeled tomato into thin strips (julienne).
Put a little clean vegetable oil in a skillet and sauté these vegetables with a little salt and pepper.
Cut chicken breasts into small pieces.
Once the vegetables are cooked, add the chicken pieces.
Stir over low heat for 3 or 4 minutes.
Place a layer of lettuce and the sautéed chicken and vegetables on the corn tortillas.
Add cream cheese (as a sauce).
Roll up the tortilla.
hints: To reduce the fat, you can use low-fat cream cheese.
To reduce the sodium, you can season the vegetables and chicken with natural seasonings such as garlic, oregano and bay leaf in place of salt.

title: Foil-Baked Cod Fillets with Peppers
description: This kidney-friendly recipe for cod fillets baked in foil with peppers is sure to be a hit when you serve it at your next meal.
ingredients: 12 ounces fresh or frozen cod fillets (thawed)
4 ounces chopped jarred peppers, no salt added
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Place two sheets of heavy-duty aluminum foil on your work surface.
Spread half of the thin lemon slices on each sheet of foil.
Place cod fillets on top of the lemon slices, 2 fillets or about 6 ounces on each sheet of foil.
Lightly sprinkle each fillet with the measured amounts of salt and pepper.
Top each fillet with chopped peppers, then drizzle with olive oil.
Fold the edges of the foil to seal the fish inside. Place on a baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes. Remove fillets from the foil to serve.
hints: Fresh roasted red peppers can also be substituted.
When adding very small amounts of salt, try combining it with pepper or other ground spices. Use a refillable salt shaker so you can distribute it evenly over the food.

title: Garden Salad
description: Garden Salad is a simple, easy-to-make salad with 5 different kidney-friendly vegetables.
steps: Tear lettuce into pieces.
Cut cabbage, celery and bell pepper into julienne strips.
Shred carrot.
Mix everything in a bowl and add one teaspoon of lemon juice or vinegar.
Serve immediately.
hints: You can replace the cabbage with cucumber or squash.
You can substitute white vinegar for the lemon juice.
